references.text: The Israelites' agreement with the ambush force was that smoke from the city would be the signal that the attack had begun, just as at Ai.
The Lord had commanded them to set the city on fire, which produced the smoke that the men of Ai saw.
Joshua and the Israelites also saw the smoke and turned to attack, while the ambush force came out of the city.
The Lord looked down from the pillar of fire and caused confusion among the Egyptians, so they could not flee—a similar situation where the enemy was trapped with no way to escape.
The Lord promised to throw the enemies into confusion and panic, so that they would not know where to flee—just like the men of Ai.
The men of Ephraim turned back on the day of battle—an example of turning in combat, as the men of Ai were forced to do.
